text.title: Accessibility-First Design Worked Example
text.summary: End-to-end example applying Accessibility-First Design to a concrete case, plus the error-state signal example, the contrast/target-size helper template, and the agentic Figma-API audit workflow for design-phase accessibility: subagent roles, JSON output schema for frame auditing, and LLM gotchas when generating or reviewing accessible designs.

section.title: Primary button + form-field tokens

example.code:
## Tokens color.fg.button.primary: #ffffff color.bg.button.primary: #1c5fdb (contrast 6.8:1 — pass) motion.button.press: 80ms (reduced-motion: none) spacing.inline-start: 12 (logical, RTL-safe)
## Archetype: button-primary role: button | focus_visible: 2px outline accent-500 | keyboard: Enter/Space → activate

section.note: Every token carries a pass marker; every archetype carries focus_visible. The system prevents SC 1.4.3 + 2.4.7 by design.

section.title: Color is never the only signal

example.note: Error state: red border + error icon + "Error:" label prefix. Three independent signals, any one sufficient.
Error state: red border only. Color-blind users see no distinction from normal state.

Figma frame audit: "For each Figma frame, output JSON: { frame_id, issues: [{ rule, severity, element_id, current, required, fix_hint }] }. Rules: contrast (4.5:1 body, 3:1 large), target_size (>=44x44), focus_visible, color_only, motion_pause, time_limit, semantic_handoff_present. Severity: blocker (WCAG 2.2 AA fail) | warn | info."
